title: Access Evidence Assembly and Retention Matrix
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview

This document defines a prescriptive workflow for collecting, assembling, classifying, and retaining access and authorization evidence across Redwood Inference services. It covers what signals to capture from RBAC systems, audit logging, model-serving requests, and private deployment telemetry, how to package evidence for compliance (ISO/ SOC / regulator requests), and a retention matrix tied to risk tiers and data residency constraints.

Intended audience
- Security engineers
- SRE and on-call responders
- Compliance and audit teams
- Dev leads responsible for entitlement and service identities

Scope
- Evidence types: access approvals, role bindings, entitlement changes, delegation handoffs, session tokens, service-account activity, authorization decision logs, and related artifacts (PRs, change tickets).
- Systems in scope: Redwood IAM (identity service), service-to-service auth logs (service-mesh), API gateway audit stream, model-serving runtime access traces, private deployment audit agents, and KMS/HSM key events.
- Exclusions: general business records (HR payroll, customer support ticket content).*

Definitions
- Evidence bundle: a logical package containing the minimum artifacts required to reconstruct an authorization event chain for a time window or incident.
- Primary artifact: the core log or record (e.g., authorization decision event, role grant operation).
- Secondary artifact: contextual items referenced by the primary artifact (PR link, change ticket, reviewer email, CI job id).
- Residency class: classification of the evidence for geographic controls (global, eu-only, customer-region).

Principles
1) Minimal yet sufficient: store the least amount of data to satisfy the audit claim while preserving forensic fidelity.
2) Immutable provenance: attribute each artifact with origin, ingestion timestamp, and cryptographic hash where possible.
3) Policy-first retention: retention time is derived from regulatory requirements, contractual SLAs, and risk tier, not from storage convenience.
4) Queryability & exportability: packaged evidence must be exportable in readable, machine-parsable formats (NDJSON/ZIP) within SLA.

Evidence assembly workflow (step-by-step)
1. Detection/Trigger (Who/When)
   - Routine: schedule daily entitlement-change snapshot job (midnight UTC).
   - Event-driven: on-role-change API or on-critical-incident alert create immediate evidence collection job.
2. Primary artifact capture
   - Capture authorization decision events from the central audit stream: fields required: event_id, timestamp, subject_id, subject_type, resource, action, decision (allow/deny), policy_version, request_context_id.
3. Secondary artifact enrichment (automated)
   - Resolve subject_id to identity provider record (idp-id, email, org unit).
   - Link request_context_id to request traces from model-serving runtime (latency, model-id, route).
   - Attach change-ticket ID (if present) and PR metadata for the code/config change that led to the policy update.
4. Packaging
   - Create an evidence bundle: metadata.json (bundle_id, assembled_at, residency_class, hash), primary.ndjson (one-line-per-event), secondary/ (files: pr.txt, ticket.json, keysnapshot.json).
5. Provenance & immutability
   - Compute SHA256 for each file; write bundle manifest signed by evidence-service signing key; write manifest record to immutable-audit-store with write-once retention TTL.
6. Tier assignment & retention policy application
   - Classify bundle into retention tier (see matrix below) and route to appropriate storage backend (regional S3, cold archive, or encrypted vault).
7. Access controls and access logging
   - Enforce least privilege for evidence retrieval; all retrievals generate an audit event and optional reviewer justification attached to bundle retrieval record.
8. Export and response
   - For auditor or regulator requests, generate an export package with redaction markers and an executive summary explaining chain-of-custody.

Retention matrix (table)
- Columns: evidence_class | examples | residency_class | retention_min | retention_max | storage_backend | access_tier
- Rows (represent as text table):
| evidence_class | examples | residency_class | retention_min | retention_max | storage_backend | access_tier |
| Authorization decisions (critical) | Deny/Allow for admin/control-plane actions | customer-region | 7 years | 10 years | encrypted-cold-vault (region) | restricted-audit |
| Entitlement changes (grants/revokes) | Role create, role-binding, delegation | global | 3 years | 7 years | regional-s3+immutable-log | restricted-audit |
| Session tokens / ephemeral creds | Temp tokens, JIT activations | global | 30 days | 2 years (hash-only) | short-term-log + hashed-index | operational |
| Service-account activity | Service identity token refresh, key rotation | eu-only / global | 2 years | 5 years | encrypted-cold-vault | restricted-audit |
| SDLC artifacts for auth changes | PRs, CI logs, approval emails | global | 3 years | 7 years | dev-archives (with hashes) | business-audit |
| Deprovision evidence | Deletion receipts, deprovision ticket | customer-region | 7 years | 10 years | regional-cold-vault | restricted-audit |

Note: retention_min = regulatory minimum; retention_max = business-driven cap. All retention values subject to legal hold (see incident response section).

Packaging checklist (minimum for a compliance-ready bundle)
- metadata.json with: bundle_id, assembled_by, assembled_at (ISO8601), residency_class, applied_retention_tier, hashes, manifest_signature_id.
- primary.ndjson (one event per line, canonicalized fields).
- context/ directory with: idp_snapshot.json (subject resolution), ticket_link.txt, pr_link.txt, model_trace.ndjson (if request-level).
- chain_of_custody.log: chronological actions taken on this bundle (who assembled, who accessed, exports).
- readme.txt: human summary and retrieval instructions.

Integration points and required fields
- Redwood IAM (identity service): include idp_user_id, external_idm_link, group_membership_snapshot_id.
- API gateway audit: include request_context_id, route, client_ip (hashed for PII-sensitive bundles), user_agent, x-forwarded-for (if present).
- Model-serving runtime: model_id, model_version, input_metadata pointer (do not include customer data payload unless justified).
- KMS/HSM events: key_id, key_event_type (rotate/create/destroy), signer_id.

SDLC & change control tie-in
- Pre-deploy gating: any change that modifies authorization policy must include: risk assessment (template), ticket id, reviewers list, and canary plan. The change must produce a post-deploy entitlement snapshot within 30 minutes of rollout.
- CI job: capture build id and artifact checksums and attach to the evidence bundle referenced by the entitlement-change event.
- Post-deploy validation: automated tests that verify policy behavior against a canonical test harness; test results are included in evidence if failure occurs.

Incident response and legal hold
1. On security incident with authorization implications, trigger evidence collection in high-priority mode (near-real-time stream backup).
2. Apply legal hold flag to all affected bundles; suspend scheduled deletion and escalate to Legal + Compliance.
3. For cross-border incidents, consult data-residency owner to determine export limits and redaction requirements before external sharing.
4. Incident exports must include chain_of_custody.log and manifest signatures to maintain admissibility.

Risk and exceptions process
- Exceptions for retention or residency must be requested via the Risk Exceptions workflow. Each request must contain: rationale, minimum data footprint required, compensating controls, expiration date.
- Approvers: Security Director OR Legal counsel (for cross-border) AND Data-residency owner for region-specific exceptions.
- All exceptions are recorded in the exception register with automated reminders for re-review 30 days before expiry.

Operational runbook snippets
- Assemble bundle CLI (example):
  redwood-evidence assemble --trigger event_id=AUTHZ_12345 --out /tmp/bundle_AUTHZ_12345.zip --residency eu-only
- Verify manifest signature:
  redwood-evidence verify --bundle /tmp/bundle_AUTHZ_12345.zip --key-id evidence-service-v2
- List bundles for retention_tier:
  redwood-evidence list --retention-tier restricted-audit --since 2024-01-01

Reporting & metrics (SLOs)
- Evidence assembly latency: 95th percentile under 2m for event-driven bundles (goal).
- Export SLA for auditor requests: 72 hours max for full export, 8 hours for summary + manifest.
- Retention compliance rate: 99.9% of bundles retained according to tier rules.

Ownership and contacts
- Evidence service owner: security-evidence@redwood.com (primary on-call: Security Infra team).
- Data-residency owner: data-governance@redwood.com.
- Legal and compliance contact (for holds): compliance-legal@redwood.com.

Appendix A — Example evidence manifest (abbreviated)
- manifest example (human-readable excerpt):
  bundle_id: BNDL-2026-00042
  assembled_at: 2026-01-14T16:23:02Z
  residency_class: eu-only
  files: [primary.ndjson, metadata.json, context/idp_snapshot.json, chain_of_custody.log]
  manifest_signature_id: sig-evidence-2026-v1

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions
- Q: When do we redact client_ip?
  A: For any customer-region bundle where PII protections apply, store hashed-ip rather than raw IP. See data-residency owner for region-specific guidance.
- Q: Who can request an export?
  A: Security, SRE lead, Legal, Compliance, or an authorized auditor with a signed NDA. All requests must be logged and justified.
